title: "Mobile Store Deployment Vault"
description: "What every Mobile Deployment vault field is, what it does in the store release workflow, and where to obtain its value."
updatedAt: "2026-09-18"
---

This runbook explains each field on the **Infrastructure → Mobile Deployment**
settings page (root workspace, `manage_mobile_deployment_vault` permission). The
vault holds the secrets, signing files, and CI tokens consumed by the
`.github/workflows/mobile-deploy-stores.yaml` workflow that builds and publishes
the Flutter mobile app to the Google Play and Apple App stores.

Each field on the settings page has an inline help tooltip with a short summary
and the console URL; this page is the full reference with clickable links.

## How The Vault Is Organized

The Infrastructure deployment must have the existing `ENCRYPTION_MASTER_KEY`
that encrypted the vault's data keys. Link the team's shared variable to the
Infrastructure project and redeploy for environment changes to take effect.
Do not generate a replacement key for an existing vault: it would make stored
versions unreadable. A server-render error with a missing master-key message in
the deployment logs indicates this configuration is absent.

Vault administration uses the signed-in Infrastructure app session and checks
the root workspace's `manage_mobile_deployment_vault` permission. CI reads use
the separately scoped CI token and GitHub OIDC identity.

- **Secrets** — short scalar values (passwords, IDs, names) and preset
  environment variables baked into the build.
- **Files** — signing certificates, keystores, and Firebase/Play config files.
- **CI tokens** — bearer tokens the GitHub Actions workflow uses to read the
  vault. Each token value is shown only once, at issue time.
- **Overview** — readiness checks plus draft activation and rollback.

## Android Signing

| Field | What it is | Where to get it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ANDROID_KEYSTORE_ALIAS` | Alias of the signing key inside the upload keystore. | Chosen when you run [`keytool -genkeypair -alias <alias>`](https://developer.android.com/studio/publish/app-signing). |
| `ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD` | Password protecting the keystore file. | Set when generating the keystore with `keytool`. |
| `ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD` | Password protecting the private key entry (often the same as the keystore password). | Set when generating the keystore with `keytool`. |
| `android_upload_keystore` (file) | The Java keystore (`.jks`) used to sign Android release builds. | Generate with [`keytool -genkeypair -v -keystore upload-keystore.jks ...`](https://developer.android.com/studio/publish/app-signing#generate-key). |

## Google Play

| Field | What it is | Where to get it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GOOGLE_PLAY_PACKAGE_NAME` | Play application ID (e.g. `com.tuturuuu.app.mobile`); must match the Android `applicationId`. | [Google Play Console](https://play.google.com/console) → App information. |
| `GOOGLE_PLAY_TRACK` | Release track (`internal`, `alpha`, `beta`, `production`). | [Play release tracks](https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/9859348). |
| `google_play_service_account_json` (file) | Service-account JSON with Play Developer API access for automated publishing. | [Google Cloud Console](https://console.cloud.google.com/iam-admin/serviceaccounts) → create JSON key, then grant access in Play Console → Users and permissions. See the [publisher API setup](https://developers.google.com/android-publisher/getting_started). |

| Field | What it is | Where to get it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `APPLE_BUNDLE_ID` | iOS bundle identifier (e.g. `com.tuturuuu.app.mobile`). | [Apple Developer → Identifiers](https://developer.apple.com/account/resources/identifiers/list). |
| `APPLE_TEAM_ID` | 10-character Apple Developer Team ID. | [Apple Developer → Membership](https://developer.apple.com/account). |
| `APPLE_DISTRIBUTION_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD` | Password used when exporting the distribution certificate `.p12`. | Chosen by you during Keychain Access export. |
| `apple_distribution_certificate_p12` (file) | Apple distribution certificate (with private key) exported as `.p12`. | [Apple Developer → Certificates](https://developer.apple.com/account/resources/certificates/list); export from Keychain Access. |
| `apple_app_store_provisioning_profile` (file) | App Store provisioning profile (`.mobileprovision`) tying the bundle ID to the certificate. | [Apple Developer → Profiles](https://developer.apple.com/account/resources/profiles/list). |

| Field | What it is | Where to get it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `APP_STORE_CONNECT_API_KEY_ID` | Key ID of the App Store Connect API key. | [App Store Connect → Integrations](https://appstoreconnect.apple.com/access/integrations/api). |

These preset env vars are baked into the build. Custom env vars can be added but
have no built-in guidance.

| Field | What it is | Where to get it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` | Supabase project URL. | [Supabase dashboard](https://supabase.com/dashboard) → Project Settings → Data API. |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` | Supabase publishable (anon) key. | Supabase dashboard → Project Settings → API Keys. |
| `API_BASE_URL` | Base URL of the Tuturuuu platform API. | Your production web deployment URL (internal). |
| `TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY` | Cloudflare Turnstile site key for bot protection. | [Cloudflare → Turnstile](https://dash.cloudflare.com/?to=/:account/turnstile). |
| `TURNSTILE_BASE_URL` | URL hosting the Turnstile challenge page. | Your production web app URL (internal). |
| `GOOGLE_WEB_CLIENT_ID` | Google OAuth 2.0 web client ID. | [Google Cloud Console → Credentials](https://console.cloud.google.com/apis/credentials). |
| `GOOGLE_IOS_CLIENT_ID` | Google OAuth 2.0 iOS client ID. | Same Credentials page (iOS client). |
| `MOBILE_TASK_DESCRIPTION_EDITING_ENABLED` | Feature flag for rich task-description editing (`true`/`false`). | Set manually (internal). |
| `MOBILE_CALENDAR_INTEGRATIONS_ENABLED` | Feature flag for calendar integrations (`true`/`false`). | Set manually (internal). |

## CI Tokens

| Field | What it is | Where to get it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Token name | A human-readable label for a CI token the deploy workflow uses to authenticate to the vault. | Chosen by you; the token value is shown once at issue time. |

## Activating Changes

Edits land in a **draft** version. Use **Verify** to re-run readiness checks,
**Activate draft** to promote it to the active bundle the workflow reads, and
**Roll back** to return to the previous active version. Fix any readiness issues
listed on the Overview tab before activating.

## Automatic beta rollout

Mobile **Settings → What's new** reads bundled release history when the user
opens that screen. Release Please owns `apps/mobile/CHANGELOG.md` for tagged
releases. Before building an iOS beta, CI looks up earlier TestFlight patch
versions and their source workflow commits, then bundles the mobile commit
summaries for each mapped patch version into `assets/release_history.json`.
Older manual builds without a matching workflow remain listed with localized
"details unavailable" copy instead of blocking the next beta. CI logs their
version and build number for follow-up. The current build is included before
upload. Android downloads the same generated asset from the iOS job. Both apps
read the bundled result offline without a changelog API or extra database table.
The installed version and build number remain visible.

The workflow runs after relevant pushes to `production`. Retry the latest push
run for recovery; vault OIDC validation permits production pushes and the
manually dispatched review retry.
Other refs fail the preflight check.
Configure the `mobile-store-beta` GitHub environment to allow only the
`production` branch, and store the issued vault token as its
`MOBILE_DEPLOYMENT_CI_TOKEN` secret. A missing token fails the run instead of
silently skipping both publishing jobs.

Both jobs fetch the active encrypted vault bundle from
`https://infrastructure.tuturuuu.com/api/v1/mobile-deployment/bundle`, with the
CI bearer token and GitHub OIDC attestation. Signing files, private keys, and
build environment files are hydrated only into temporary runner paths and
cleaned up afterward. Do not copy signing values into repository secrets or
commit them to source. The App Store private key uses `API_PRIVATE_KEYS_DIR`.

If a bundle fetch returns 401, first confirm that the request uses
`environment=production`, a supported `platform`, and a bearer authorization
header. Invalid inputs return before the route logs a denial. For valid inputs,
check the infrastructure production request log for
`Mobile deployment bundle request denied`. Its `stage` and `code` identify where
validation stopped without recording credentials or the OIDC token. If that log
is absent, inspect the proxy or deployment edge. Vault bundle-fetch rows appear
only after OIDC validation and admin-client setup have succeeded.

Each workflow run assigns both platforms the build number
`100000 + GITHUB_RUN_NUMBER * 1000 + GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT`. Retrying a job receives
a fresh number. Release Please continues to own the marketing version. Retry
the newest release workflow rather than an older source revision after a more
recent build has already been published.

Android uploads a signed AAB to the **internal** track with completed status.
The verification step reads that track using a temporary Play API edit and
requires the exact version code. It deletes the edit without committing it.

iOS validates the profile's expiration, exact team and bundle ID, App Store
distribution type, and production push entitlement. CI uses a temporary
keychain and an ignored `ios/Flutter/StoreSigning.xcconfig` for manual
distribution signing. Export uses the profile UUID and App Store Connect export
method. Local development keeps its existing signing settings when that file
does not exist.

Create an internal TestFlight group with automatic distribution enabled. After
upload, CI waits up to 30 minutes for the exact build to become valid and
available for internal testing. It then assigns the build to all existing
TestFlight groups, including external groups, and reads the assignments back.
An accepted upload alone does not pass verification. New groups are discovered
on each run, so future groups are included by default.

The `mobile-store-beta` GitHub environment accepts two optional variables:

| Variable | Default | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `TESTFLIGHT_BETA_ENABLED` | `true` | Set `false` to skip automatic group assignment. The internal group's own automatic distribution setting still applies. |
| `TESTFLIGHT_BETA_GROUPS` | `all` | Comma-separated exact group names or App Store Connect group IDs to limit assignment. Unknown names fail the run. |
| `TESTFLIGHT_BETA_WHATS_NEW` | Generic test note | English (U.S.) instructions shown to external testers when a new build is submitted for beta review. Set this to specific test areas for a release. |

External groups require TestFlight beta review before testers can install a new
build. If an external group is selected, CI creates a missing English (U.S.)
What to Test localization, enables automatic tester notification, and submits
the build for beta review. A workflow success with `WAITING_FOR_REVIEW` or
`IN_REVIEW` confirms submission, not external tester availability. Confirm
Apple's approval and external testing status in App Store Connect. Keep the
app's beta review contact and app description current there. Missing export
compliance, processing failures, and internal distribution must also be
resolved in App Store Connect.

Apple permits only one external beta build in review at a time. The review
queue checks every five minutes and dispatches the production retry workflow;
it leaves an existing review in place and submits the newest eligible build
when that review ends. GitHub's scheduled runs can start late, so this is a
best-effort interval rather than a guaranteed five-minute submission time.

Run focused release checks with `node --test scripts/mobile-deployment/*.test.mjs
scripts/ci/mobile-store-workflow.test.js`. Use `ttr resources run -- bun check`
for repository validation and `ttr resources run -- bun check:mobile` for the
Flutter checks. Store availability still requires an authenticated release run
with the active production vault and real signing assets.

## Device authenticator smoke checks

Open Settings → Session → Device authenticator. Setup opens above the shell in
a dismissible phone sheet or tablet dialog; test both orientations, keyboard
visibility, Close and system Back. Enroll only on a device with local identity
verification configured. Verify registration, a generated code, and a second
device approval separately from successful store upload.

The devices API uses explicit JWT assurance checks for stateless mobile Bearer
requests. A cookie-session-only assurance lookup returns no level for those
clients and can reject confirmation after the provider activates the factor.
An interrupted setup resumes from its account-scoped secure credential; never
clear secure storage as a troubleshooting shortcut. Retry repeats the failed
operation. Error messages distinguish network, session, rate-limit, service
unavailability, and cancelled local verification without exposing provider
payloads or credentials. Simulator biometric support varies by runtime; passing
widget tests does not establish real-device biometric approval.

## Live audio regression checks

The mobile app overrides `record_ios` with the licensed local copy in
`apps/mobile/vendor/record_ios`. The patch rejects zero-channel or zero-rate
input formats before installing an audio tap, returning a recoverable platform
error instead of an uncaught Core Audio exception. Keep this guard when updating
the recording dependency and test unavailable inputs on the simulator, plus
real microphone and headset routes on a physical device.

Live chat history is read server-side only after verifying that the caller owns
the chat. Test denied ownership and failed ownership lookup before any privileged
message access. The seed includes at most the latest 200 messages in stable
chronological order. Deploy the API fix before treating a mobile-only build as
proof of a working Live session.

### Updating one credential and repairing an older draft

The production sync workflow applies
`20260923120000_mobile_vault_draft_inheritance.sql`. Verify that migration and
the updated application deployment have completed before repairing or activating
a draft; do not run a separate direct production SQL push. New drafts
inherit the active version's credentials under a fresh envelope key before edits
are accepted. An interrupted initialization can be retried; it cannot be used as
an editable partial draft.

For a draft created by the previous implementation, open Infrastructure → Mobile
Deployment → Overview and choose **Inherit missing credentials**. This is an
explicit administrator mutation using the same permission and CSRF checks as
other vault changes. It retains existing draft values, including an updated
provisioning profile, and preserves recorded deletions and `.env` replacements.
Legacy deletions are reconstructed from the old audit history; if that history
is incomplete, review the missing-resource list before repair. Repair is a
one-time operation per active source, not a fallback on every read.

Inheritance decrypts only inside the server, checks plaintext and ciphertext
hashes, and re-encrypts under the draft key. Files receive separate immutable
attempt paths, and ordinary credential uploads also use unique encrypted paths
so concurrent uploads cannot overwrite one another's file bytes. Database
metadata is committed atomically with a draft revision check; concurrent edits
cause a conflict rather than replacement of new values.
After a conflict, refresh and retry. Verify readiness, then activate the draft
before triggering the store workflow.

Preparation failures clean up their own attempted uploads. An ambiguous network
failure during the final database commit can leave unreferenced encrypted attempt
files. Do not delete these merely because the HTTP request failed: first confirm
whether metadata committed and ensure no inheritance request is still running.
Only unreferenced `inherit-*` files in that draft's reserved vault directory may
be reclaimed. Never remove active-version or currently referenced artifacts.

## Live screen-sharing extension

Live screen sharing uses Android MediaProjection and an iOS ReplayKit Broadcast
Upload Extension, rather than camera capture or an app-only screenshot. The
operating system asks the user to choose and authorize the capture session. Live
shows a stop control; Android also exposes a persistent stop notification and
iOS retains its system broadcast indicator. Android adds the microphone foreground
service type only while the existing, user-authorized Live microphone is active,
and removes that type when muted; screen sharing itself can continue muted.

On iOS, an active Live microphone session is required before screen sharing. The
real voice session keeps the host's audio transport running while the user opens
other apps; muting it stops screen sharing. No silent background-audio workaround
is used. The extension stores only the latest bounded JPEG in a protected App
Group directory, with a short host heartbeat and random capture-session ID. No
account token, Live token, history, or capture archive crosses into the group.
Frames are removed after delivery and capture stops if the host stops responding.

Full iOS broadcast signing requires App Group
`group.com.tuturuuu.app.mobile.live` on both the Runner identifier
`com.tuturuuu.app.mobile` and extension identifier
`com.tuturuuu.app.mobile.LiveScreenBroadcast`. Regenerate the Runner App Store
profile in the encrypted Infrastructure vault with that entitlement, and put the
separate extension App Store profile into the `mobile-store-beta` environment's
`APPLE_BROADCAST_PROVISIONING_PROFILE_B64` encrypted secret. Keep that profile
available for a later build with the extension. Never weaken mobile OIDC to
export a signing key or reuse a Runner profile for the extension.

App Store Connect rejected build 207001 with error 90362 even though the signed
IPA contained `NSExtension.NSExtensionAttributes.RPBroadcastProcessMode` set to
`RPBroadcastProcessModeSampleBuffer`. While Apple rejects the extension, the
production TestFlight workflow removes Runner's extension dependency and embed
phase only in its CI workspace with
`scripts/mobile-deployment/omit-broadcast-extension.rb`. It builds with
`IOS_LIVE_SCREEN_BROADCAST_ENABLED=false` so iOS Live does not offer an unusable
screen-sharing control. The workflow verifies the exported IPA has no broadcast
extension before uploading it. Android sharing and local iOS builds retain
their source configuration. To restore iOS TestFlight broadcast, restore its
profile mapping, extension signature checks, and Dart build flag together, then
verify that Apple accepts the signed IPA and that a physical iPhone can stream.

The project membership helper uses Swift and XcodeProj:

```sh
swift run --package-path scripts/mobile-live-project mobile-live-project apps/mobile/ios
```

Run it through the shared resource queue after changing native membership. The
extension has its own build configuration and does not link Runner's Flutter or
CocoaPods libraries. Development/staging identifiers use their own corresponding
App Groups and signing profiles.

Before marking screen sharing validated, check physical Android and iPhone/iPad devices: grant and
cancel system consent, switch apps, rotate, stop from system UI, mute on iOS,
change account/workspace, reconnect Live, and lock/unlock the device. Confirm the
assistant receives the selected screen and that no frames continue after stop.
Simulator tests and passing Dart tests do not prove background broadcast delivery.
